Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Indemnity language (IP claims)

Thanks for the redlines, Karthik — quick note from Acme legal. We cannot accept a broad customer indemnity back to Redwood for third-party IP infringement covering our own code or pre-existing integrations. Our position is:

- Acme will not indemnify Redwood for Redwood-originated IP claims.
- We can accept a narrow obligation around customer-provided content (e.g., materials, data, customer ML models) where applicable.
- If Redwood wants a wider IP indemnity, we need either escrow for source or a clear cap and an express obligation for Redwood to take first responsibility for remediation or replacement.

I attached a short workbook with our comments next to each indemnity clause for reference. Please let us know if Redwood can propose a middle-ground that limits Acme exposure while giving Redwood remedies for genuine third-party claims.

[Attachment: Acme_Indemnity_Notes.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

Best,

Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and the workbook. Valuable context.

Short answer: Redwood cannot remove customer indemnity entirely for third-party IP claims that arise from customer-supplied content or instructions that cause an infringement (e.g., customer uploads a licensed dataset that infringes). That said, we're open to a focused compromise that:

- Limits customer indemnity to customer-supplied materials and configurations;
- Preserves Redwood's obligation to defend and indemnify for claims arising from our models, services, or code; and
- Adds a reasonable cap and notification/control mechanics.

I’m looping in our legal lead to propose concrete language so we can close the MSA and get the Order Form signed.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Karthik / Markus — see attached redline and summary positions. Key guidance for negotiation:

1) Customer indemnity: narrow to "Customer Content" and "Customer Instructions" only. Do not accept upstream customer-created derivatives unless they expressly represent ownership.
2) Redwood indemnity: Redwood will defend and indemnify for (a) infringement by the Redwood platform and models as delivered, and (b) misuse of third-party licensed models where Redwood’s distribution is the proximate cause.
3) Control of defense: Redwood should have the right to assume defense with a covenant to keep the customer reasonably informed. We can offer to reimburse reasonable settlements.
4) Cap & insurance: propose an indemnity cap equal to 1x the annual fees for the implicated Order Form, and a mutual carveout where either party’s liability for IP claims is subject to available insurance coverage.
5) Carveouts: disclaimers for open-source claims, customer modifications, and combined product claims where the alleged infringement arises from customer code.

Attached: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf (high level redline) and a 1-page summary we can send to Acme.

Let me know if you want us on the next thread with Acme legal. If Karthik agrees, send the summary compromise and we’ll include the PDF redline for review.

- Lauren
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - allocation of liability for third-party IP claims

Samantha — thanks again and appreciate the workbook. We discussed internally with legal and have a compromise proposal below (high level). Attached is a 1-page plain-language summary to share with your team. If that reads OK, we’ll incorporate the specific redlines in the MSA and circulate an updated Order Form for signature (DocuSign link included).

Proposed compromise (high level):
- Customer indemnity: Acme will indemnify Redwood only for third-party claims to the extent they arise from Customer Content or Customer Instructions (definitions to be added). This excludes claims attributable to Redwood’s models, pre-built connectors provided by Redwood, or Redwood-managed infrastructure.
- Redwood indemnity: Redwood will defend and indemnify Acme for third-party IP claims alleging that the Redwood platform or our hosted models infringe, subject to the exclusions below.
- Control & cooperation: Redwood may elect to assume defense with counsel of our choice; Redwood will provide prompt notice and regular updates. Acme will cooperate and may participate (at its expense) if it chooses.
- Cap: For third-party IP indemnity claims, liability will be capped at the greater of (i) the fees paid under the Order Form for the prior 12 months or (ii) the proceeds of relevant insurance coverage; not to exceed USD 2,000,000 in aggregate per claim (negotiable).
- Carveouts: No indemnity for (i) claims based solely on Customer modifications, (ii) open-source license compliance claims where the Customer is the distributor, and (iii) combined usage where the infringement is primarily due to customer code.
- Notification: Acme to notify Redwood within 30 days of becoming aware of a claim; failure to notify will only relieve Redwood to the extent Redwood is materially prejudiced.

Next steps: please confirm whether Acme can accept the bullets above. If yes, we will send the redlined MSA and the updated Order Form via DocuSign for signature. DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABCDEF-123456

[Attachment: summary_indemnity_compromise.txt (TXT, 3KB)]

Thanks,
Karthik
